Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for applicant in the Court today, is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for informant as well as learned A.G.A for the State and perused the record 3.

This bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant-accused in Case Crime No.273 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police station Gahmar, District Ghazipur, with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.
4. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is husband of deceased.

sentences.text: Only general allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against all the accused persons, including the applicant.
It was stated that applicant was working in Dubai and he has returned back to Delhi on 20.12.2023 and while he was coming to Ghazipur, he came to know that deceased has committed suicide.
At the time of incident, applicant was not present at the spot.
In post mortem report, except ligature mark, no other injury has been shown on the body of the deceased and the cause of death is ante mortem hanging.

Lastly it has been submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 27.12.2023, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
5.

Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for informant have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of deceased and there is evidence that deceased was harassed by applicant and his family members on account of dowry.
It was submitted that applicant was present at the spot and information regarding the incident was also given by the applicant.
It was stated that there are serious allegations against him.

6. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant- Om Prakash Sahani involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate any of the prosecution witness.
iii. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
8. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
